_comment: The app set the nightly canary proves as one candidate set and the public install draws from. `github` is the app's gate of record (the GitHub repo, since 2026-09-30; LastGit is retired): last-stack-canary-candidate-set reads each app's main from it, writes it as the candidate-set `source` that last-stack-install-apps --pins clones from, and `next` rows carry it. An app that has not moved keeps `lastgit` (lastdb:///<repo>) and `forge` (the frozen Forgejo copy); the candidate set tries `github`, then `lastgit` when git-remote-lastdb is on PATH, then `forge`. `public` is the source `stable` rows carry (GitHub, what an outside user installs from; no LastGit needed). `artifact_app` names the LastGit artifact CAS channel whose source_oid is the app's released head. `install_name` is the directory last-stack-install-apps uses under ~/lastdb-apps. `requires` lists bundle apps an app cannot run without (last-stack-install-apps warns on a gap); `recommends` lists bundle apps that only add a feature. Every app also needs the LastDB daemon, which the bundle installs from Homebrew, so lastdbd is not listed. Full map: docs/app-dependencies.md. `brew_apps` are public Homebrew binaries from the edgevector/lastdb tap (source private): last-stack-install-apps installs them with brew, and the canary candidate set does not pin them.
